q1: SELECT ACTOR_ID,DIRECTOR_ID FROM ACTORDIRECTOR GROUP BY ACTOR_ID,DIRECTOR_ID HAVING COUNT(*)>=3
q2: SELECT ACTOR_ID,DIRECTOR_ID FROM ( SELECT COUNT(*) CNT,ACTOR_ID,DIRECTOR_ID FROM ACTORDIRECTOR GROUP BY ACTOR_ID,DIRECTOR_ID HAVING CNT >= 3 ) FYI
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT ACTOR_ID,DIRECTOR_ID FROM ACTORDIRECTOR GROUP BY ACTOR_ID,DIRECTOR_ID HAVING COUNT(*)>=3
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT ACTOR_ID,DIRECTOR_ID FROM ( SELECT COUNT(*) CNT,ACTOR_ID,DIRECTOR_ID FROM ACTORDIRECTOR GROUP BY ACTOR_ID,DIRECTOR_ID HAVING CNT >= 3 ) FYI
explanation: Both Q1 and Q2 aim to retrieve pairs of (ACTOR_ID, DIRECTOR_ID) from the ACTORDIRECTOR table where the count of occurrences (grouped by ACTOR_ID, DIRECTOR_ID) is at least 3. Q1 uses HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3 directly in the outer query, while Q2 uses a subquery with an alias for the count and then filters in the outer query. Since both use the same grouping and same count condition, they are semantically equivalent.
